newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Re sees M&G, PartnerRe boosting EPS.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Re sees M&G, PartnerRe boosting EPS.

text.p: Swiss Reinsurance Co expects newly acquired life and health specialist Mercantile & General Re together with a raised stake in PartnerRe to add between nine and 12 Swiss francs to earnings per share (EPS) this year.
Swiss Re chief executive Walter Kielholz said the profits would be in addition to last year's EPS of 100 Swiss francs.
But he added that a simple addition would not yield this year's expected EPS figure because of possible changes in other profit sources in the course of 1997.
"We expect the first-time consolidation of M&G's business in 1997 to contribute between six and eight Swiss francs in earnings per share," Kielholz told a news conference.
Kielholz said the profit boost would be based on higher operating profits in life and health reinsurance.
Synergies in this area would have a stronger effect on earnings in 1998, he added.
Restructuring costs for the M&G integration were already contained in provisions taken on 1996 results, he said.

Kielholz said raising Swiss Re's stake in Bahamas-based PartnerRe would add three to four Swiss francs to 1997 EPS, a number which he also expected to grow in 1998 after the deal is completed in mid-1997.
The complicated deal involves buying up all of France's Societe Anonyme Francaise de Reassurances (SAFR) and selling it to PartnerRe in return for a capital gain of 100 million Swiss francs.
Swiss Re's stake in PartnerRe will also grow to 21.8 percent from an earlier 11.1 percent.
